summary: Kim Plofker is a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. She studied at Haverford College (~1981–1985) and Brown University (~1989–1995) under David Pingree. She held posts at Union College, MIT, and the American Oriental Society.

Kimberley C. Patton is a religious studies scholar who completed her dissertation at Harvard University (~1992). Her career includes posts as an associate at the American School of Classical Studies at Athens (1991) and assistant professor at Harvard (~1991).

Kimiaki Tanaka is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1974–1983) and under Ratnakaji Bajracharya. He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Keio University, Toho Gakuin, and Eastern Institute.
Kimmo Koskenniemi is a linguist who studied at Helsingin Suomalainen Yhteiskoulu (until ~1964). He served as Professor of Computer Linguistics at the University of Helsinki from ~1989 to 2012.

Kin Cheung is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Temple University (~2011–2017). His doctoral studies were supervised by Shigenori Nagatomo, alongside committee members Marcus Bingenheimer and Shanyang Zhao.

King Chung Lo is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at Leipzig University (2009–2018) under doctoral supervisor Eli Franco and committee member Vincent Eltschinger.
King Pong Chiu is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Manchester (~2009–2014), completing a Doctor of Philosophy under supervisor Jacqueline Suthren Hirst.

Kirin Narayan is a religious studies and Indology scholar. She studied at Sarah Lawrence College (~1974–1978) and UC Berkeley (~1980–1987), later holding posts at Hampshire College, Middlebury College, the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1989–2012), and Australian National University (~2012).
Kisari Mohan Ganguli was an Indologist who completed studies at Presidency University, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta.

Kisor Kumar Chakrabarti is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who studied under traditional teachers and instructors including Madhusudana Nyayacarya, Visvabandhu Tarkatirtha, and Gopinath Bhattacharyya. He held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Kitaro Nishida was a philosopher and religious studies scholar educated at Ishikawa Normal School, Fourth Higher School, and Tokyo Imperial University. He held posts at several schools before serving as Professor of Philosophy at Kyoto University (1912–1927).

Kiyoaki Okuda is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies under Ludwig Alsdorf (~1968–1973). He has served as a professor at Shitennoji University and director at the Shitennoji Doctrinal Research Institute.

Kiyoshi Kato was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Enga Teramoto and earned a BA at Otani University (1931). He held positions at Higashi Honganji (1935) and Hyangsam Vocational Girls' School (1938).
Kiyoshi Okano is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bhikkhu Pāsādika. He held an associate professorship in humanities at Kyushu University from ~1996 to 2002.
Kiyoshi Shimokawabe is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Rissho University and subsequently held a post there as a special research member.

Kiyotaka Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology educated at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Tsurumi University, the University of Tokyo, and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Kiyotaka Yoshimizu is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at the University of Tokyo and under Gerhard Oberhammer. His academic career includes positions at Hokkaido University (~1993–1997), Tohoku University (~1997–2019), and Toyo Bunko.

Kiyozo Kazama is a linguistics and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Vienna, under Naoshiro Tsuji. He held academic posts at Hosei University, Nagoya University, and the University of Tokyo (~1976–1989).
Klaus Bruhn was an Indologist who studied under Ludwig Alsdorf (~1950–1954). He served as a professor at the Humboldt University of Berlin from ~1966 to 1994.

Klaus Butzenberger is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1984–1991) and served as Lehrstuhlinhaber at the University of Tübingen (~2004–2009).
